newsitem.title: UK: PowerGen drops as letter hits profit hopes.
newsitem.headline: PowerGen drops as letter hits profit hopes.

text.p: Shares in PowerGen Plc dropped in early trading on Monday after a report in the Financial Times said a letter from the company to analysts had led to sharp cuts to earnings forecasts.
The stock was down 6p at 610 by 0712 GMT while rival power generator National Power Plc was down 3p at 502-1/2.

The FT said the letter, described as a "pre-closed season" list of pointers, had highlighted a range of "key analyst forecasts" which was well below the top end of the range of expectations, which had been as high as 660 million stg.
It quoted an unnamed analyst as saying he had lowered his forecast for the company's pre-tax profit for the year to March 31, 1997 to 580 million stg from 650 million.
However the paper added that the letter suggested power generators had had a good year with total generation up three percent.
It said some analysts argued that PowerGen was holding over some of its fiscal 1997 profits in advance of further deregulation of the electricity market due next year.
A spokesman for PowerGen had no immediate comment on the report.
